chunks: If you desire I can give you a third example of Dāwūd (a.s.). He is the holder of the Psalms and the reciter among the people of Paradise. He used to prepare baskets of date palm leaves with his own hands and would say to his companions : “Which of you will help me by purchasing it?” He used to eat barley bread (bought) out of its price.

key_terms.قَارِىءِ أَهْلِ الْجَنَّةِ: Reciter among the people of Paradise

ai.seo_question: What did Prophet David (Dawud) do with his hands and how did he support himself?
ai.summary: This narration from Nahj al-Balagha illustrates the Prophetic model of combining spiritual authority with manual labor, emphasizing that dignity lies in self-sufficiency rather than status. It serves as a practical guide for the Shia tradition, encouraging believers to engage in honest trade and avoid dependency, mirroring the humility of Dāwūd (AS) who sustained himself through his own hands.
